summary: Tensor audit complete. For extremal k-AP-free counts r_k(n), slicing gives only r_k(mn)≤min(m*r_k(n), n*r_k(m)); patterns in fibers need not align. The checked k=3 witness r_3(3)=2 and r_3(9)≥5 via {0,1,3,7,8} disproves direct submultiplicativity. The square-block estimate r_k(q²)≤q(q−1)−1 yields lim r_k(n)/n≤1−(q+1)/q²<1, but no decay under iteration. Any diagonal approximate tensor bound r_k(n²)≤r_k(n)²+o(n²), or normalized-error product inequality, would be genuinely stronger: subadditivity gives α=lim r_k(n)/n, then α≤α² and α<1 force α=0. Proving vanishing cross-fiber error is a new density-increment/removal-type step absent from one-block counting. Notes recorded in RESEARCH.md; no new Lean code.
